subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should the durable inbound-decoration contract be an OpenClaw-owned serialized metadata field, and which existing owner should create it when inbound metadata is added?
rationale: The branch currently introduces generic top-level fields but no authoritative producer; choosing the persistent ownership boundary determines the safe repair and compatibility contract.

options.title: Use an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope
options.body: Recommended: create and persist the trusted decoration record at the inbound-decoration owner, keeping generic message fields and plugin-facing shape unchanged.

options.title: Accept top-level message fields
options.body: Keep `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as serialized top-level fields, but document their owner, permitted writers, and compatibility contract before adding the missing producer.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Pause this PR until the related clean-body/plugin contract direction is settled, then implement one shared producer and reader shape.

recommendation.title: Use an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope
recommendation.body: Recommended: create and persist the trusted decoration record at the inbound-decoration owner, keeping generic message fields and plugin-facing shape unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the canonical report that identifies the ownership decision, though current code-history ownership could not be established from the supplied review context.
